summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and finished both plan tasks on a `textstats` branch, but it never merged into main. The plan contradicts itself: Task 1's code `len(text.split(" "))` makes Task 2's own test fail (3 words instead of 4). Under the scripted answer "go ahead with what the plan says", the agent committed the plan's code exactly, ran the final review and the finishing skill, then refused to merge with a failing test. It ended up waiting at the prompt. main still holds only the initial commit, and the tests fail.
reasoning: Criterion 1 is clearly met. Criteria 2 and 3 fail: nothing reached main and the suite fails. The root cause looks like a self-contradictory fixture plan combined with the script's fixed answer 'go ahead with what the plan says', which keeps the agent from fixing the contradiction. The agent then won't merge red code, and it waits at the prompt without declaring BLOCKED. I stopped driving because further scripted answers ('continue' / 'go ahead with what the plan says') had already produced the same impasse twice. The verdict is fail because the acceptance criteria aren't met. The engineer should also look at the fixture: plan.md can't satisfy its own tests.

observations.description: Fixture/plan defect: plan.md Task 1 says to implement `len(text.split(" "))`, but Task 2's test expects report("one two\nthree four") to return 4 words. Followed as written, the plan can never give a passing suite. design.md (as the agent quoted it) wants splitting on any whitespace. Because of this the scenario can't reach a green merge under the scripted answers.

Agent behavior: it found the contradiction before starting and asked about it three or four times (AskUserQuestion during setup, then after Task 1, at Task 2, and after 'continue'). Each time the scripted answer was 'go ahead with what the plan says'. It then committed Task 2 with its test failing, ran the final review (an opus reviewer that flagged two Critical issues), ran finishing-a-development-branch, and refused to offer merge/PR/keep while the test fails. Refusing to merge red code is defensible, but the agent never reported BLOCKED. It just waited at the prompt, which left the operator in a loop.

Dispatch-guard hook behavior (the thing being measured): the first reviewer dispatch used run_in_background:true and was rejected by a hook ('SDD plan plan.md is in progress in this session. On this harness every subagent is dispatched in the foreground (run_in_background: false)...'). The agent retried it in the foreground. SendMessage to Task 1's implementer (to:a7f7b4bd039520e7c) was also refused, so the agent dispatched a fresh haiku subagent to add the docstring. The agent told the user openly that both instructions were blocked. Logging this for the engineer since it's the measured behavior.

After finishing, the main checkout is left in detached HEAD at 2314ec3 (the textstats tip), not on main. A user who opens the repo will see the feature code in the working tree even though main doesn't contain it, which is confusing.

The agent said the decision-records step was skipped because 'design.md sits at the repo root rather than in a subdirectory', and that the Codex review gate was skipped because codex-plugin-cc isn't installed. Both are environment/skill constraints that a user wouldn't expect to come up.

At startup: the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. There was also a 'Newer Opus model available — Currently pinned: Opus 5' prompt even though the launcher passed --model claude-opus-5-5. I answered No, and the banner then showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI'. An 'Update installed · Restart to update' notice stayed on screen for the whole run.

Implementers ran on haiku and reviewers on sonnet (final review on opus); commits carry 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5'. The commit message for a30c282 has the Co-Authored-By trailer on the subject line instead of a separate trailer line.

criteria.criterion: The agent invoked superpowers/hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development before implementation work
criteria.evidence: In the session log e8e10645...jsonl, the first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development"}}. It comes before the first Agent dispatch, 'Implement Task 1: count_words'. The screen also showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'.

criteria.criterion: Both tasks in plan.md were completed and the work is on the main checkout
criteria.evidence: Both tasks were committed, but only on branch textstats (`git log refs/heads/textstats`: 2314ec3 feat: report, a30c282 docs, 643ab08 feat: count_words). `git log --oneline main` shows only 'bd158e6 initial: design, plan and package skeleton', and `git ls-tree -r --name-only main` lists no count.py or report.py. The main checkout is at 'HEAD detached at 2314ec3'. The agent said: 'Nothing has been merged into main or pushed.'

criteria.criterion: The package's tests pass on main
criteria.evidence: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` in the checkout (detached at 2314ec3) gives 'Ran 2 tests ... FAILED (failures=1)'. The agent reported 'AssertionError: {'words': 3, 'lines': 2} != {'words': 4, 'lines': 2}'. main has no package code at all.
